title: Atomic Structure
text: Atoms consist of protons (positive, in the nucleus), neutrons (neutral, in the nucleus), and electrons (negative, orbiting the nucleus). The number of protons defines the element (atomic number).

title: Periodic Table Groups
text: Elements in the same group (column) of the periodic table share similar chemical properties because they have the same number of electrons in their outer shell.

title: Ionic vs Covalent Bonding
text: Ionic bonds form when electrons are transferred between atoms (typically metal + non-metal), creating charged ions. Covalent bonds form when atoms share electrons (typically non-metal + non-metal).

title: Acids and Bases
text: Acids release H+ ions in solution and have a pH below 7. Bases release OH- ions and have a pH above 7. pH 7 is neutral. The pH scale runs from 0 to 14.

title: Balancing Chemical Equations
text: A balanced chemical equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides, reflecting the law of conservation of mass — matter is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction.

title: States of Matter
text: Matter exists mainly as solid, liquid, or gas. Melting turns solid to liquid, boiling/evaporation turns liquid to gas, and the reverse changes are freezing and condensation.

title: The Mole Concept
text: A mole is a unit representing 6.022 x 10^23 particles (Avogadro's number). Moles = mass / molar mass, and is used to relate mass to number of particles in chemistry calculations.
